note: The replaced test told the originals apart by name; name is one register-level fact, so a second name would stop ANSWER forming at all. They differ here in their operational definition, a delivery-level text the pin covers. Each also carries its own Datatyp, so the projected type shows which original moved: the pinned CVID 20 (int, read as integer) to 2016, CVID 21 (varchar, read as text) left in 2009. CVID 20 is delivered second, so a first-delivered selection picks the wrong one.
fails_if: `compile_occurrence_corrections` selects originals by column and edition alone, by delivery position, or picks the original whose prose does not match the pin, so CVID 21 moves to 2016 (or both move, or the entry is refused as ambiguous)

sources.description: Edition 99 (2009) delivers ANSWER twice for variable 5: first CVID 21, with operational definition 'Distinct ninth event' and Datatyp varchar, then CVID 20 with the fixture's default prose and Datatyp int.
